title: Non-blocking findings from frontend-cftc-cot-display's PR review (#407)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #407 (frontend-cftc-cot-display), recorded here per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges. (That review also found one blocking issue -- a tie-handling bug in describeExtreme -- which was sent back to task-worker on the PR itself rather than deferred here.)

checklist.step: frontend/src/features/cftc/components/cftcCotHelp.ts's describeExtreme type predicate (`market[pick] !== null`) only excludes `null`, not `undefined`, even though CFTCCOTMarketOut's `*_cot_index_52w` fields are typed `number | null | undefined` (an optional-and-nullable Pydantic field). If a market object ever had the field actually `undefined` (key omitted) rather than explicit `null`, the predicate would wrongly type-narrow it to `number` and the subsequent `.toFixed(0)` call would throw. Currently unreachable in practice -- the backend has no `response_model_exclude_none`, so it always serializes an explicit `null` -- so this is a latent defensive-coding gap, not a live bug. `features/stocks/components/metricHelpContent.ts`'s own `isKnown` helper (`value !== null && value !== undefined && !Number.isNaN(value)`) already establishes the right null+undefined-safe pattern for this exact shape elsewhere in the codebase; bring describeExtreme's filter in line with it (and add a test exercising an explicit `undefined` value, not just `null`).
